name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: French 10-year yield fell to 4.8% on 23 Nov, off its October 24-year high of 5.1%; no failed G7 auction found
state: The French 10-year yield fell to 4.8% on 23 Nov as President Macron floated a constitutional budget rule, still about 125bp higher this year but below October's 24-year high of 5.1% (Trading Economics). France's November flash PMI showed its sharpest contraction in six months. No confirmed sustained France–Bund spread above 150bp, failed G7 auction or emergency central-bank buying was found as of 24 Nov, so the Alert is unconfirmed and Watch holds.
for_you: Higher government borrowing costs in France and other G7 states tend to feed through to mortgage and business lending rates and can squeeze public spending plans.
rubric_hit: Watch: France–Bund spread in or near the 80–150bp band; no failed G7 auction, emergency buying or confirmed spread >150bp

sources.title: Trading Economics — French bond yields fall as Macron weighs constitutional budget rule

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
